title: Retinal Artery Occlusion
verification: Article page read in full on 2026-11-08; assigned editor Neelakshi Bhagat, status 'Up to Date' as of 2026-08-15. Verbatim: 'The central retinal artery, the first branch of the ophthalmic artery, is the main blood supplier of the inner layers of the retina. After entering the eye, the central retinal artery divides into superior and inferior branches. In addition, the cilioretinal artery is a branch of the short posterior ciliary arteries...This artery supplies the choroid and the outer retinal layers.' Cilioretinal artery sparing CRAO: cilioretinal artery is fed by short posterior ciliary arteries; preserves central vision in a subset of CRAO eyes.

title: Clinical Manifestations and Visual Prognosis of Cilioretinal Artery Sparing Central Retinal Artery Occlusion
verification: Full article read on PMC 2026-11-08. Among 90 eyes with complete CRAO, cilioretinal-sparing CRAO was 17.8% (16/90); mean initial BCVA (2.04 +/- 0.69 vs 2.34 +/- 0.47, p=0.039) and final BCVA (1.65 +/- 0.87 vs 2.22 +/- 0.84, p=0.001) were significantly better in cilioretinal-sparing group. Poor visual outcome (final BCVA <20/200) was 81.3% in cilioretinal-sparing vs 97.3% in non-sparing group (p=0.01). Papillomacular bundle ischemia at onset was associated with poor vision (12/13 [92.3%] in poor vision group vs 1/3 [33.3%] in good vision group, p=0.016).

publisher: Progress in Retinal and Eye Research

title: Papilledema
verification: Article page read in full on 2026-11-08; assigned editor Danah Albreiki, status 'Update Pending' last review 2024-12-10. Verbatim: 'Papilledema results from orthograde axoplasmic flow stasis at the optic nerve head, leading to edema of the nerve from the increased intracranial pressure on the nerve behind the eye. Continued pressure can result in loss of axons and eventual optic atrophy secondary to intraneuronal ischemia, ultimately causing vision loss.' Increased ICP is transmitted via the subarachnoid space surrounding the optic nerve.

title: Blood-retinal barrier
verification: Full abstract read on Europe PMC 2026-11-08 (cited by 775). 'The BRB consists of inner and outer components, the inner BRB being formed of tight junctions between retinal capillary endothelial cells and the outer BRB of tight junctions between retinal pigment epithelium cells.' 'Diabetic retinopathy is initiated by an alteration of the inner BRB and neovascular AMD is a result of an alteration of the outer BRB.'

verification: Citation verified on PubMed / FEBS Press 2026-11-08: review of the iBRB (retinal capillary endothelial tight junctions) and oBRB (RPE tight junctions), the supporting role of pericytes, astrocytes and Mueller glia of the retinal neurovascular unit, and the two barriers maintaining the regulated retinal microenvironment.
